children: plans to eliminate 1,070 positions across its headquarters and air division, seeking voluntary departures as it reorganizes to respond faster to customers. Manufacturing workers and aircraft maintenance staff will be excluded.
For investors, the restructuring highlights BAE’s

focus on efficiency after years of expansion driven by rising defense budgets. The company still expects underlying operating profit to grow 10% to 12% in 2026, although union concerns about delayed U.K. spending underline the importance of turning government commitments into contracts.

employs about 50,000 people in Britain, compared with 35,000 six years ago. Its air business, which includes fighter-jet production, accounts for 18,500 employees, while headquarters employs approximately 1,000.
The company described the reductions as part of an investment plan intended to improve competitiveness and meet government demands for quicker delivery amid changing security threats.

Trade union Unite blamed delays in British defense spending for pressure on industry employment. It urged the government to place orders for Typhoon fighters and collaborative combat aircraft to protect jobs and support growth.

title: BAE Systems plans 1,070 job cuts despite defense spending boom
